macro.title: Fed Rate Path Uncertainty Ahead of June Decision
macro.body: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold rates steady in June but markets are pricing in a possible 25 bps hike later in the year. Higher rates would keep Treasury yields elevated, pressuring USD‑heavy positions and amplifying decay in 3x leveraged equity ETFs.
macro.bull: If the Fed pauses, leveraged long ETFs like SPXL could benefit from a continued equity rally.
macro.base: A hold scenario keeps yields stable, limiting further decay but also limiting upside.
macro.bear: A surprise hike would push yields higher, widening CAD‑USD spread and hurting leveraged long positions.

macro.title: Global Inflation Pressures from Energy Supply Disruptions
macro.body: Recent drone attacks in the Middle East and the delayed restart of Saudi pipelines have introduced short‑term supply constraints, nudging global oil and gas prices upward. Higher energy costs feed into CPI readings worldwide, sustaining inflation expectations.
macro.bull: Energy‑linked equities and commodity‑sensitive stocks could see price support.
macro.base: Inflation remains elevated but without a sustained shock, keeping markets range‑bound.
macro.bear: Persisting price spikes could trigger tighter monetary policy globally, hurting growth‑oriented tech holdings.

macro.title: China’s Accelerated LNG Import Program
macro.body: With the Iran‑US conflict de‑escalating, China, India and Pakistan are set to increase LNG imports, supporting global demand for liquefied natural gas. The incremental demand is modest relative to overall supply but could buoy North American LNG exporters.
macro.bull: Canadian LNG exporters may see marginal price support.
macro.base: Demand growth is incremental, unlikely to move markets dramatically.
macro.bear: If demand stalls, LNG prices could slip, pressuring related equities.

news.headline: Boeing and Korean Air seal 103‑aircraft order
news.body: The order boosts aerospace manufacturing outlook, directly benefiting Boeing (BA) and its supply chain. While the portfolio holds no aerospace stocks, the increased demand for high‑tech components could lift semiconductor makers like QCOM and AVGO.

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Supply chain ramps up, driving higher orders for chips used in avionics.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Order proceeds without broader sector ripple.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Delays or cost overruns dampen component demand.

news.headline: Saudi coalition reports Houthi drone destroyed near Mecca
news.body: Escalation in the Red Sea raises geopolitical risk premium for oil. Saudi pipeline restart is still pending, keeping supply tight. ENB.TO, a major Canadian energy producer, stands to benefit from higher crude prices.

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Oil prices climb 2‑3% as supply concerns linger.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Pipeline resumes soon, limiting price upside.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Rapid de‑escalation eases premiums, oil retreats.

news.headline: Wells Fargo reports improvement in key credit metric
news.body: Improved credit quality at a major U.S. bank signals resilience in the financial sector. The portfolio’s Canadian bank exposure (CM.TO, RY.TO, BMO.TO) could see modest upside if U.S. banking stability translates north.
news.exposure: CM.TO ~$8K CAD, RY.TO ~$7K CAD, BMO.TO ~$6K CAD

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Cross‑border credit sentiment lifts Canadian banks.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Banks trade within range, limited impact.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Unexpected U.S. credit deterioration spills over.

daily_outlook: Today's mix of geopolitical tension in the Middle East and a major aerospace order creates a modestly bullish bias for energy and semiconductor exposures, while the Fed's pending rate decision keeps leveraged equity positions vulnerable to volatility spikes.

risks.title: Leverage Decay Risk – 3x ETFs in Elevated Volatility
risks.context: 49% of portfolio (~$137K CAD) in SPXL, UDOW, FNGU
risks.body: With VIX trading above 22, daily rebalancing drag can erode returns on leveraged ETFs, especially if markets swing sharply. The portfolio’s outsized exposure magnifies both upside and downside, but decay risk dominates in sideways or volatile environments.

risks.title: FX Translation Drag on USD‑Heavy Holdings
risks.context: ≈68% of portfolio value (~$190K USD) denominated in USD
risks.body: A CAD appreciation beyond the current 1.3925 rate would reduce the CAD value of USD‑denominated assets, directly impacting leveraged positions and tech stocks. Recent Treasury yield moves add pressure to the CAD/USD pair.

risks.title: Earnings Concentration in AI‑Chip Mega‑Cap Cluster
risks.context: Top 6 tech holdings (NVDA, AVGO, QCOM, TSM, MSFT, AAPL) represent ~20% of portfolio value
risks.body: Quarterly earnings volatility in this cluster can cause outsized swings. Any miss on guidance or regulatory setback could disproportionately affect portfolio performance.

picks.thesis: Pembina Pipeline offers stable cash flow and a 5.5% dividend yield, providing CAD‑denominated income to offset FX exposure and diversify away from high‑beta tech.
picks.entry: Target entry around $30‑$32 CAD per share; watch for quarterly earnings (Q4) and any pipeline capacity updates.

picks.thesis: Caterpillar benefits from global infrastructure spending and a rebounding construction cycle, adding a defensive industrial exposure that is less correlated with tech and leveraged ETFs.
picks.entry: Consider buying on pull‑backs near $260‑$275 USD; monitor U.S. construction PMI and Fed policy signals.

strengths.text: Low average cost basis across holdings, with many positions (e.g., NVDA) acquired at deep discounts relative to current market.
Strong historical ROI (+83% overall) demonstrates effective growth orientation and timing.
Tax‑advantaged FHSA balance (~$55K CAD) growing at 123% provides a future down‑payment source free of tax.
RRSP balance (+72% ROI) shelters future growth and generates foreign tax credits for U.S. dividend income.
Diversified sector mix: tech, Canadian financials, energy, and leveraged equity exposure gives upside potential across market regimes.

concerns.text: Uninvested cash in the RRSP (~$15K CAD) is subject to cash‑drag, especially as the portfolio seeks higher returns.
Overlap between leveraged ETFs and core tech holdings creates correlated risk during market corrections.
Liquidity constraints on some leveraged ETFs could widen spreads during rapid market moves.
Upcoming non‑resident tax filing (2026) may trigger deemed disposition rules and affect RRSP contribution timing.
High concentration in USD assets exposes the portfolio to CAD appreciation risk without natural hedges.

strategy_short.text: Monitor the Fed’s June rate decision; if yields rise further, consider modestly trimming SPXL/FNGU exposure to limit decay risk.
Implement a small CAD‑USD hedge (e.g., 1‑yr forward) for the USD‑heavy portion to mitigate translation drag.
Deploy idle RRSP cash into PPL.TO to generate dividend income and add CAD‑denominated exposure.

strategy_mid.text: Rebalance the portfolio toward lower‑beta Canadian equities (e.g., financials, utilities) to reduce correlation with tech volatility.
Gradually replace a portion of leveraged ETF holdings with a broad market index fund (e.g., VTI in the Investment account) to lower volatility while preserving growth.
Increase RRSP contributions in 2027 to capture additional foreign tax credits before the non‑resident year ends.

strategy_long.text: Build a core Canadian dividend portfolio (e.g., BCE, ENB, RY) within the FHSA and RRSP to provide stable, tax‑efficient income for the long‑term home‑purchase goal.
Phase out high‑leverage ETFs over the next 3‑5 years, reallocating proceeds to inflation‑protected securities (e.g., BMO Real Return Bond Index) to preserve purchasing power.
Plan a strategic conversion of a portion of the RRSP to a TFSA after returning to residency (post‑2027) to lock in tax‑free growth on the accumulated gains.

tax.text: RRSP contributions reduce taxable income; ensure you stay within the 2026 contribution limit (~$29K CAD) before the non‑resident year.
Foreign tax credits can be claimed for U.S. dividend withholding on holdings like NVDA and AAPL, offsetting Canadian tax liability.
When you become a non‑resident in 2026, any RRSP withdrawals will be subject to a 25% withholding tax unless a tax treaty applies; plan withdrawals after re‑establishing residency.
Capital gains realized within the TFSA remain tax‑free; avoid moving new purchases into TFSA this year due to the FHSA suspension and non‑resident status.

macro_history.title: US Treasury Yield Surge Signals Higher Global Funding Costs
macro_history.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent noted that 10‑year yields are climbing above 4.5% as fiscal deficits widen and global risk appetite wanes. Higher yields raise borrowing costs for corporations and governments worldwide, pressuring equity valuations and increasing the cost of carry for leveraged ETFs in the portfolio.
macro_history.bull: If yields stabilize below 4.6%, the credit spread compression could support risk assets.
macro_history.base: Yield volatility remains moderate, keeping leveraged exposure roughly flat.
macro_history.bear: A breakout above 4.7% could trigger a sell‑off in high‑beta tech and leveraged positions.

macro_history.title: Escalating Iran‑War Costs Heighten Geopolitical Risk Premium
macro_history.body: The Congressional Budget Office estimates the Iran conflict is now costing $38 billion per month, with expenditures rising. Persistent conflict raises oil price volatility and could disrupt global trade routes, affecting commodity exporters and energy stocks in the portfolio.
macro_history.bull: If diplomatic de‑escalation occurs, oil markets could settle, benefitting Canadian energy producers.
macro_history.base: Current conflict level likely persists without major escalation.
macro_history.bear: Further escalation or sanctions could spike oil prices and trigger broader market risk‑off, hurting high‑beta tech holdings.

macro_history.title: Saudi Pipeline Restart Expected Within Days, Boosting Global Oil Supply
macro_history.body: Saudi Arabia’s main crude pipeline is slated to resume operations, adding roughly 1 million barrels per day to the market. The added supply may temper price spikes, influencing Canadian oil producers and LNG exporters.
macro_history.bull: Increased supply could lower oil prices, reducing cost pressures for ENB.TO and supporting its dividend sustainability.
macro_history.base: Supply addition likely modest relative to global demand trends.
macro_history.bear: If the pipeline faces further delays, oil prices could stay elevated, increasing volatility for leveraged equity positions.

macro_history.title: US Fiscal Deficit Fuels Higher Treasury Yields
macro_history.body: The widening U.S. fiscal gap has pushed 10‑year Treasury yields toward 4.5%, widening the CAD‑USD spread. Higher yields tend to strengthen the dollar, which will increase the CAD cost of the portfolio’s 68% USD‑denominated exposure.
macro_history.bull: If the dollar stabilises after a short‑term rally, the CAD‑USD spread narrows, reducing translation drag on USD‑heavy holdings.
macro_history.base: Yield levels hover around current highs, keeping the CAD‑USD spread modestly elevated.
macro_history.bear: A sustained rise in yields could push the CAD deeper into the 1.42‑1.44 range, amplifying translation losses on the USD‑heavy core.

macro_history.title: China’s Post‑War LNG Import Surge
macro_history.body: With the US‑Iran conflict de‑escalating, China, India and Pakistan are expected to boost LNG imports, supporting global gas prices. Higher LNG spot rates benefit Canadian producers and exporters, notably ENB.TO, which has exposure to natural‑gas pipelines and LNG contracts.
macro_history.bull: Rising LNG prices lift ENB’s cash flow and dividend sustainability.
macro_history.base: Gas prices remain volatile but trend modestly higher, offering limited upside.
macro_history.bear: If demand softens or supply rebounds, gas prices could slip, pressuring ENB’s earnings.

macro_history.title: Canadian Export Weakness Dampens Q3 Growth Outlook
macro_history.body: Statistics Canada’s revised Q3 GDP estimate shows a slowdown, driven by weaker commodity exports. Slower growth can curb domestic equity demand and keep interest rates elevated, which hurts high‑beta, leveraged equity exposure.
macro_history.bull: If the slowdown is temporary, rate‑sensitive sectors could rebound, supporting the broader market.
macro_history.base: Growth remains modest, keeping equity valuations flat.
macro_history.bear: Prolonged export weakness could trigger a rate‑hike cycle, increasing volatility and decay risk for 3x ETFs.

macro_history.title: OPEC+ Extends Production Cuts Into 2027
macro_history.body: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies announced an additional 1.2 million‑barrel‑per‑day cut through the end of 2027, supporting crude prices amid lingering demand concerns. Higher oil prices tend to boost energy equities and Canadian energy exporters, while also pressuring inflation globally.
macro_history.bull: Energy stocks and inflation‑linked assets rally, lifting the value of Canadian energy holdings.
macro_history.base: Modest price support for oil keeps energy sector stable without major upside.
macro_history.bear: Persistently high oil prices fuel cost‑of‑living pressures, prompting tighter monetary policy and a risk‑off shift.

macro_history.title: China's May Manufacturing PMI Surges Above Expectations
macro_history.body: China reported a manufacturing PMI of 52.3, its strongest reading in eight months, suggesting a modest rebound in industrial activity. While the effect on North American markets is limited, it may ease concerns about global demand for semiconductors and commodities.
macro_history.bull: Improved Chinese demand supports global chip makers and commodity exporters.
macro_history.base: Limited direct exposure means the impact remains muted.
macro_history.bear: If the rebound stalls, sentiment could turn negative for tech and commodity cycles.

macro_history.title: EU Announces New Digital Services Tax on Large Tech Platforms
macro_history.body: The European Union voted to impose a 3% digital services tax on revenues of major online platforms, targeting companies like Microsoft, Apple, and Amazon. The policy could increase cost‑of‑doing‑business for North American tech firms and affect earnings forecasts.
macro_history.bull: If companies absorb the tax without passing costs to users, earnings impact may be limited.
macro_history.base: The tax is modest relative to overall revenue, likely resulting in a small earnings drag.
macro_history.bear: Higher effective tax rates could compress margins and trigger a sector rotation away from high‑growth tech.

macro_history.title: Fed Rate Hike Anticipation Tightens US Credit Markets
macro_history.body: The Federal Reserve is expected to raise its policy rate in the upcoming meeting, driven by persistent core inflation and a widening fiscal deficit. Higher rates will lift US Treasury yields, pressuring USD‑heavy assets and increasing the cost of capital for growth‑oriented firms.
macro_history.bull: If the hike is modest and markets view it as a pre‑emptive move, equity volatility may ease, supporting leveraged tech exposure.
macro_history.base: A standard 25‑bp hike with no surprise shock leads to modest market adjustment.
macro_history.bear: A larger‑than‑expected hike could trigger a risk‑off rally, hurting high‑beta tech and leveraged ETFs.

macro_history.title: Canadian Q3 GDP Growth Slows Amid Export Weakness
macro_history.body: Statistics Canada reported a 0.7% QoQ growth for Q3, down from 1.3% in Q2, reflecting weaker commodity exports and a softening housing market. Slower growth may keep the BoC cautious on rate cuts, sustaining a modest CAD‑USD spread.
macro_history.bull: If the slowdown is viewed as temporary, the CAD could stabilize, limiting FX drag on USD‑heavy holdings.
macro_history.base: Continued modest growth keeps the BoC on hold, leaving current FX levels largely unchanged.
macro_history.bear: Persistent weakness could push the BoC to tighten, widening the CAD‑USD spread and hurting USD‑denominated positions.

macro_history.title: CRA Announces Expanded Foreign Income Reporting for Non‑Residents
macro_history.body: Effective Jan 2027, the Canada Revenue Agency will require detailed reporting of foreign‑source investment income for Canadians who become non‑residents. This adds compliance complexity for RRSP and Investment accounts holding US‑denominated securities.
macro_history.bull: Early compliance may allow strategic re‑allocation into Canadian‑listed ETFs, reducing future FX exposure.
macro_history.base: Most investors will adjust filing processes without major portfolio disruption.
macro_history.bear: Unexpected penalties for late reporting could erode after‑tax returns on USD assets.
